articles.title: Brushed Cross
articles.summary: Bidirectional H+V cross-brushed strata with scattered '+' cross marks as hero motif, fine scotch-brite sheen. A uniform satin-metal haze with a faint glitter; no visible direction or marks.
articles.what: R6 rebuild: bidirectional H+V cross-brushed scotch-brite strata + 100-200 explicit '+' cross marks 8-16 px scattered as HERO motif (no more engine-turn circles) + 14-22 l Up close: A fine sandy scotch-brite grain with a light dust of pin-point bright specks and a few tiny plus-shaped marks scattered thinly. No streak direction is readable; it reads as an even dull abrasive haze. From a distance: A uniform satin-metal haze with a faint glitter; no visible direction or marks. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Directional Metal & Brush (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, hood, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Directional Metal & Brush", or search for "Brushed Cross".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof and doors on a metallic base
Splitter and spoiler for a worn-metal look
Hardly visible: a few dim specks
Pairs well with: matte, satin, metallic.
pitfalls: Not Brushed Linear or Diagonal: there are no long streaks here, only fine grain
Not a red paint despite the 'red' tag: it adds no colour
Avoid: chrome base that hides the brush, very busy liveries.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.goal: Layer Brushed Cross over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Brushed Diagonal
articles.summary: 45° diagonal brushed lines, chevron-style panel polish, even fine roughness streaks across the surface. Reads as a smooth satin metal with a faint directional grain; the 45-degree brush direction only becomes obvious across a whole panel.
articles.what: 45° diagonal brushed lines via rotated projection — chevron-style panel polish, G=Roughness Up close: Finely dotted, broken line grain with a few wide faint vertical dark bands, about 30 px wide, sitting in the shadow area. In the highlight, rows of tiny bright dots align in a loose diagonal grain; no solid streaks are visible at this crop. From a distance: Reads as a smooth satin metal with a faint directional grain; the 45-degree brush direction only becomes obvious across a whole panel. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Directional Metal & Brush (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.

articles.title: Brushed Linear (Cool)
articles.summary: Crisp high-frequency linear brush grain; tight parallel streaks catch light as a cool satin sheen. A directional satin-metal grain with soft vertical streaking; reads as a cool brushed steel sheen.
articles.what: Cool-toned brushed_linear — crisper higher-frequency grain with boosted contrast, suits steel/titanium/chrome finishes, G=Roughness Up close: Vertical streaking: soft wide dark vertical bands about 20-30 px wide in the shaded area and tiny bright dash-like specks in the highlight, with a few vertical wavering stripes crossing it. Crisper than a plain brush but still sparse at this crop. From a distance: A directional satin-metal grain with soft vertical streaking; reads as a cool brushed steel sheen. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Directional Metal & Brush (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Directional Metal & Brush", or search for "Brushed Linear (Cool)".

Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof and doors on a metallic base
Splitter, mirrors and spoiler for a machined metal look
Numbers stay legible; grain is subtle under them.
Faint: soft streaks and a few specks, easily missed
Pairs well with: chrome, metallic, gloss, matte.
pitfalls: Not Brushed Diagonal: this runs vertical here, with higher contrast
Not a colour: 'cool' means crisper grain, not blue paint
Avoid: too coarse for large body panels, reads flat under matte base.
